Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment: Acute focal neurological deficit with left arm weakness, dysarthria/dysphagia, and left facial tingling; onset about 1 hour ago; vascular risk factors included (type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension). High concern for acute ischemic stroke; emergency evaluation and transport to hospital indicated. Ambulance arrangements in progress; patient is alone at home and asked to keep front door accessible; clinician will remain on call to coordinate.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx, integrated):
  - Acute ischemic stroke — High
  - Acute hemorrhagic stroke — Moderate
  - Hypoglycemia — Moderate
  - Transient ischemic attack (TIA) / evolving stroke — Moderate
  (Note: No conflicts between transcript and DDx; no additional items added beyond DDx consistent with transcript.)

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded
  - Ambulance transport to local hospital / A&E for acute stroke evaluation and possible treatment
  - Maintain safety: front door open or accessible; patient to stay on line with clinician until arrival
  - No home investigative or therapeutic steps beyond ensuring rapid hospital assessment

- Dietitian referral:  consider_dietitian_or_not_recorded
- CTG registration (if not enrolled):  consider_ctg_or_not_recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute ischemic stroke — High
  - Rationale: Sudden onset left arm weakness with dysarthria/dysphagia; risk factors (DM2, HTN); symptoms within a 1-hour window; clinician identified stroke possibility.
- Acute hemorrhagic stroke — Moderate
  - Rationale: Hypertension; abrupt neurological presentation; lack of imaging confirmation.
- Hypoglycemia — Moderate
  - Rationale: Diabetes on metformin with acute neuro symptoms; otherwise not typical for focal unilateral weakness; no typical hypoglycemia symptoms documented.

- Transcript quality (e.g., noisy/inaudible segments):  transcript_quality_summary
